candidates.excerpt: The Port of Coos Bay has secured nearly $205 million in federal funding to upgrade its rail line, advancing a proposed Oregon container terminal that would rely on trains to move cargo between ships and inland markets. The $204.8 million award, announced Oct. 19 by Oregon Sens. Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden and Rep. Val Hoyle, will fund final design and construction of improvements to the Coos Bay Rail Line. The work is intended to increase capacity, improve reliability and prepare the railroad to support the proposed Pacific Coast Intermodal Port, or PCIP. The funding comes through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) grants program. Planned improvements include repairing and replacing track, ties, bridges and tunnels, according to Hoyle’s office. The 111-mile railroad runs from Coos Bay to near Eugene. candidates.title: MBTA board approves purchase of new Siemens locomotives
candidates.excerpt: BOSTON — The Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority board of directors on Thursday unanimously approved the purchase of 20 Siemens Charger locomotives — 10 diesel-electric units and 10 dual-mode battery-catenary electric hybrids — for $310.4 million. William Wolfgang, the MBTA’s senior director of vehicle engineering, told the board the agency “has, obviously, an immediate need for locomotives.” Delivery of the diesels would begin in mid-2029 and continue through the following year, with the battery-electrics arriving in 2030 and 2031. The new locomotives will replace the oldest locomotives in the MBTA fleet, GP40s built more than 50 years ago and F40s that are 33 to 39 years old. A presentation to the board said that 13 of the GP40s have exceeded their useful life, while the F40s will reach the end of their life between 2029 and 2035. candidates.title: NSR vs Suez: the Arctic is not a tradelane, it’s a corridor with a hefty premium
candidates.excerpt: Shippers stressing over risks from Suez Canal and Red Sea transits The return of Asia-Europe container shipping services to routing via the Red Sea and Suez ... Two sets of numbers have landed in the same week. On 19 October, data from Norway’s Centre for High North Logistics (CHNL) showed 104 ships had crossed Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) by 30 September, already more than in all of 2025. Four days earlier, Lloyd’s List Intelligence reported that containerships moved 2.19m teu through the Suez Canal last month, the most since the Houthi campaign began, and Linerlytica expects carriers to be fully back to Suez by the first quarter of 2027. Most coverage reads the first as proof that the Arctic is finally opening, but read together, they say something else: the part of the NSR Moscow planned and paid for has missed its targets by a wide margin, while the part it barely planned for has beaten them, because other people’s chokepoints closed. candidates.title: Is the Red Sea safe?
candidates.excerpt: Is the Red Sea safe? An accelerating return of container shipping to the Suez Canal, Red Sea and Bab El Mandeb, amid an escalating and widening conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis is raising industry concerns. Are crew and cargoes at risk? For almost three years, since the latest conflict in the Middle East began, container shipping lines have diverted their vessels around the Cape of Good Hope. Some tentative attempts were made to return to the far shorter Red Sea route earlier this year, but the US war on Iran stalled the return to Suez Canal transits. Since the summer, however, an accelerated return to the far shorter route has seen some 63% of pre-war capacity return to the route which bisects North and East Africa to the west and Saudi Arabia and Yemen to the east. Increased tensions in the region, particularly between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis, are again causing anxiety amongst industry organisations, except it seems the shipping lines. candidates.title: New York short line wins $11.2 million federal rail grant
candidates.excerpt: Ontario Midland Railroad has secured an $11.2 million federal grant to rehabilitate approximately 10 miles of track in Wayne County, New York, improving infrastructure that supports the region’s agricultural and manufacturing shippers. The Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project will replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight grade crossings, replace seven turnouts and remove three others. Work also includes ballast placement, tamping and track surfacing, according to an Oct. 19 announcement from the railroad and U.S. Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand. The award comes through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements, or CRISI, program. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. candidates.excerpt: Intramotev will deploy two autonomous freight railcars on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad as part of a project supported by a $16.2 million federal grant awarded to the City of Columbia. The Federal Railroad Administration selected the city for funding under its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program, according to the announcement. Intramotev will serve as the technology partner, deploying its TugVolt technology on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia.
